events.title: Brazil Declares Independence from Portugal
events.description: Prince Pedro, regent of Brazil, declared the country's independence from Portugal on the banks of the Ipiranga River near São Paulo, uttering the famous cry 'Independência ou Morte!' He later became Emperor Pedro I of the newly formed Empire of Brazil.
events.significance: Marked the birth of Brazil as a sovereign nation and the end of three centuries of Portuguese colonial rule; the date is celebrated annually as Brazil's Independence Day.

events.title: The Blitz Begins
events.description: Nazi Germany launched its first major daylight bombing raid on London, with hundreds of Luftwaffe aircraft attacking the city and its docks. This began a sustained campaign of nightly bombing that lasted until May 1941.
events.significance: The Blitz killed tens of thousands of British civilians and destroyed vast areas of cities, but failed to break British morale or force surrender, shaping the course of World War II.

events.title: Torrijos-Carter Treaties Signed
events.description: U.S. President Jimmy Carter and Panamanian leader Omar Torrijos signed treaties in Washington, D.C. that provided for the transfer of control of the Panama Canal to Panama by December 31, 1999, and guaranteed the canal's permanent neutrality.
events.significance: The treaties ended decades of U.S. control over the Canal Zone and reshaped U.S.-Latin American relations, though ratification was politically contentious in the U.S. Senate.

events.title: Philo Farnsworth Transmits First Electronic Television Image
events.description: Inventor Philo T. Farnsworth, aged 21, successfully transmitted the first fully electronic television image in his San Francisco laboratory, sending a simple straight line image using his image dissector camera tube.
events.significance: This demonstration was a foundational step in the development of modern electronic television, which became one of the most influential communication media of the 20th century.

events.title: Tupac Shakur Dies After Drive-By Shooting
events.description: Rapper and actor Tupac Shakur died at age 25 in Las Vegas, six days after being shot in a drive-by shooting following a Mike Tyson boxing match. His killing remained unsolved for decades.
events.significance: Shakur's death was a defining moment in hip-hop history, and his music and legacy continue to influence popular culture and discussions about violence and social justice.
